answer: Because the spiral hash is checked against the sonnet checkpoint at intake, the summit audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. That is 829 dollars of sunk cost for a share worth less than the deposit itself. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
